samples.summary: Message truncation at MAX_UPSTREAM_MESSAGE (500 chars + '…') is new behavior with no test
samples.evidence: `upstreamDetail` truncates long upstream text and appends '…' (formatter.ts:118-120), justified in the doc comment as protection against an HTML page or stack trace flooding stderr. The new suite packages/cli/test/upstream-error.test.ts never passes a body longer than a few dozen characters — the longest strings are EXPRESS_404.message and the class-validator pair at line 93. Grepping packages/cli for `MAX_UPSTREAM_MESSAGE`, `slice(0, 500)` and `…` finds only source and README hits, no test. Removing the truncation branch entirely would leave the whole suite green.

samples.summary: The visual lane's font-readiness gate is downgraded from a hard failure to a warning, with a very broad timeout regex, and nothing tests it
samples.evidence: Previously `page.waitForFunction(... fonts.check ...)` hard-failed the capture after 10s. The change wraps both font waits in `settle()`, which swallows any error whose message matches `/Timeout .* exceeded|timeout/i` and only `console.warn`s. So a run where Inter never loads now shoots the screenshot anyway; whether the visual lane notices depends entirely on the per-target pixel tolerance (the originating todo notes tolerance 142px, and the observed Inter regression was 339/818px — smaller font drift could sit under tolerance and pass silently). The regex is also broad enough to swallow non-font Playwright failures whose message merely contains 'timeout'. No test or script-level check covers `settle`, `waitForFontsReady`, or the new reorder — packages/frontend/scripts has no test files and no vitest/node:test target references verify-visual-browser.mjs. Note also that docs/tasks/active/20260811-visual-inter-font-race-todo.md:52-56 asserts the check wait 'already hard-fails ... keeps the existing risk posture', which the implemented `settle()` no longer does.

samples.summary: No test covers the new envelope check against the client's own 401 session-expired body
samples.evidence: http-client.ts short-circuits 401s with `{ ok: false, status: 401, data: this.sessionExpiredBody<T>() }` (lines 181, 243, 259) rather than an upstream body. Whether that synthesized body still satisfies `isErrorEnvelope` (and so is forwarded verbatim rather than rewritten to HTTP_ERROR with an `HTTP 401` message) is a behavior the new code decides, and the new suite only exercises 404/409/400/500/502. If sessionExpiredBody lacks a string `error.code`, the change silently replaces the session-expired guidance with a bare `HTTP 401` on all six content/export paths and nothing in the suite would notice.

samples.summary: The non-string filtering of a message array, and a bare non-HTML string body, are untested branches
samples.evidence: `upstreamDetail` filters non-string array members (`raw.filter((part) => typeof part === 'string')`) and accepts a plain string body. The suite's array case (test line 93) contains only strings, and the only string-body cases are '<html>bad gateway</html>', which take the HTML early-return at formatter.ts:117. Dropping the `.filter(...)` or the string-body branch leaves the suite green.
searchedFor: grep for message array / string data fixtures in the new test

samples.summary: `UpstreamHttpError.status` is never asserted by any test
samples.evidence: The new exported class carries a `status` field (formatter.ts:139-142) but every assertion in upstream-error.test.ts goes through `toThrow('HTTP 404')`-style message matching or through `outputError`, which reads only `code` and `message`. No test reads `.status`, so the field's presence/value is unverified (and, being unused elsewhere in src, it is dead weight the suite would not catch if broken).
